01 / The challenge

The challenge for dog groomers.

A mobile grooming van is the salon. It parks outside customers’ homes for an hour or more, so it is a great advert for the street, and pet owners love a friendly, fun design.

01

The van is the shop

You do not have a shopfront. The van has to do all the branding.

02

Parked for hours

Neighbours see the van for the whole appointment.

03

Standing out

Mobile groomers are popular. A memorable design wins repeat bookings.

02 / What to include

What your van must say.

  • Business name
  • Mobile dog grooming
  • Services, e.g. bath, trim, nails
  • Phone number and booking website

Not sure what to include? Our guide to what to put on a work van walks you through it.

04 / Recommended package

A playful full or partial wrap.

Bright colours, paw prints or a friendly illustration. A full wrap works well for a van that is parked all day.

06 / Design tips

Build the layout around the job.

01

Use a friendly illustration

A cartoon dog or your own dog photo helps people remember you.

02

Show the services

A short list such as bath, trim and nails helps customers know what you offer.

03

Make booking easy

A website or social handle for booking reduces phone calls while you work.

Before you book

Good to know.

Can you use a photo of my own dog?

Yes. Send a high-resolution photo and we will check it works at size.

Full wrap or partial wrap?

A full wrap makes the most impact. A partial wrap works if your van colour suits your brand.

Can you work around the side door and vents?

Yes. Send photos so we can plan around the conversion.
